commits.message:
fix(launch): drain bytes count as read and pipe errors count in either phase (candybar-testing-0x6u.yzt)

Second high review of #595. A capture knows its category and stats from the
start, so a read error is counted whether or not the stream is drained, and a
drain's dropped bytes show while it is still open. A drain's end is one value.
Comments no longer claim the launch's scope goes at settle, or that only a
descendant outside the group is drained.

fix(launch): a captured pipe's read error is counted for its whole life, not only once drained (candybar-testing-0x6u.yzt)

Medium review of #595. The drain tests assert end kinds, not bytes a group-end
settle may move, and the abort case proves the holder's pipe is destroyed.

fix(launch): a launch's drained pipes have one owner, one bound and a stat (candybar-testing-0x6u.yzt)

A pipe a descendant holds past its launch is read by the launch's own capture
for its whole life: one byte count against MAX_CAPTURED_BYTES, cut past it so a
chatty holder dies at its next write. The launcher holds every open drain,
destroys them when its scope closes, and meters draining/drainedBytes/drainsCut
into the subprocess stats. Settle drops the child's listeners, so the launch's
closure and output go with its result.

fix(url-handler): the app is replaced whole, EPIPE is reported not fatal, and the doctor parses an old daemon's arrivals (candybar-daemon-health-ajx0.co4)

From the second high review. Install assembles and signs the app beside
its place and renames it over the old one, so a failed sign leaves the
handler the user had. The forwarder sets SO_NOSIGPIPE, so a daemon that
ends the socket mid-write is an EPIPE it logs, not a SIGPIPE that ends
the app silently. The doctor's CLI probe parses each arrival off the
daemon's stats and tells a daemon from before the forwarder (no
delivery) apart as skew instead of dereferencing it. The set of frame
versions the daemon speaks is derived from the current version, and the
connection declares `waits` above the backstop that reads it.

fix(url-handler): a url frame is answered to no one, the app writes a long frame whole, and install resolves the forwarder before staging (candybar-daemon-health-ajx0.co4)

From the medium review. The connection no longer writes a url frame's
answer: its writer closed by design, and on a real socket the write was
only an error event logged as a warning per click. The Swift app loops
its write with a bounded poll, so a link longer than the socket buffer
lands whole instead of being dropped as a short write; the link is
private in the unified log, since a copy link carries the text copied.
Install resolves the forwarder before the runtime is staged, so a
checkout with no build fails with nothing half done. The doctor's row
for a click request says what it knows (not the forwarder) and leaves
naming the applet to the opener's row. The doctor e2e test forwards as
the app does: one frame, hang up, read the click event.

fix(connection): a url frame stays in flight under the deadline, and the connection classifies the frame once (candybar-daemon-health-ajx0.co4)

The forwarder hangs up after its write by design. The connection treated
that close as a vanished peer: it cleared the request backstop and left
in-flight while the click was still queued, so a forwarded click had no
deadline (a repeat click could revert a toggle) and stats under-counted.
Now the connection classifies the inbound frame once (Inbound), passes it
to the daemon, and for a url frame keeps the backstop and the in-flight
count until the click is handled, with no client said to have left.

Also from the high review: install's platform-package lookup is one
helper for the render entry and the forwarder; check-protocol refuses a
row naming no mirror by label; the spawn-category docs name codesign and
killall instead of the retired osacompile and plutil.
test(click-event): the click event's via field is expected on every click (candybar-daemon-health-ajx0.co4)

feat(url-handler): a resident Swift forwarder sends the raw link to the daemon, which does all parsing (candybar-daemon-health-ajx0.co4)

The URL handler app is a Swift agent (url-handler/main.swift) that forwards each
cc-candybar:// link as one url frame, versioned by itself, and reads no answer.
The daemon classifies inbound frames once, splits the verb itself, and writes a
click event for every url frame, refused ones included. clientVersion leaves the
wire; a click's arrival carries who delivered it, and the doctor judges by that.
Install assembles the .app around the prebuilt binary, ad-hoc signs it, quits the
resident instance and registers the scheme. CI builds a universal binary on macOS
into both darwin packages; check-protocol pins the Swift frame and socket path.
url-handle remains the tmux status line's route only.
fix(test): a render is held past the request backstop by a pipe the test writes, not by a compile's speed (candybar-testing-0x6u.8vd)

fix(test): the frame-feed cases run on one held clock (candybar-testing-0x6u.fs0) (#596)

* fix(test): the frame-feed cases run on one held clock, so no draw count reads real time (candybar-testing-0x6u.fs0)

Every case in test/frame-feed.test.ts built its feed on the system clock, a
per-describe jest fake, or a busy-wait, so a stalled CI loop skipped a turn
and failed an exact draw count. The harness now owns a heldClock and returns
it; a case moves time with clock.advance, and a render that takes renderMs
burns that much of the clock (new HeldClock.burn), so a render slower than its
period runs back to back instead of looping at one held moment. HeldClock also
gains pending() and never moves time back after a burn. Loose bounds that only
a loaded box needed are the exact counts the periods give.

* fix(test): a repeating held timer runs once after a burn, a held span is refused unless finite and non-negative (candybar-testing-0x6u.fs0)

* docs(test): advance names its inclusive end and the clock a burning callback carries past it (candybar-testing-0x6u.fs0)
